--- CHUNK 1 ---
From Palembang under date 24th October in the year 1694: experience assists. Always maintain a watchful eye on the activities of Pang Rato, and likewise against any undertaking of Pringabaija, without trusting either of them in the slightest; you are also instructed that upon occurrence of the one or the other to give notice as speedily as shall be possible. with which under the wish of wholesome success I remain with great respect (signed) your service willing friend (was signed) W[illia]m Bolton, on the side In the Dutch Company: Palembang the 4th August in the year 1694. secret. Palembang To the Esteemed: Willem Bolton Merchant, and chief Resident. Earnest, prudent, and very discreet From your esteemed letter under date 4th August last, as well as from the further enclosures, which came secretly into my hands in the Company's common letter, it has become sufficiently clear to me how much trouble their High Worshipful Excellencies at Batavia have taken with the examination of the envoys both from Pringabaija as well as from Pang Rato, in order once to discover the means by which the Jambian [Jambi] miserable condition might be restored or at least its ruin might be prevented and averted: but upon all this nothing being found, except for the last mentioned P[rince] S[outh] Aagje the fortune

To the most noble Lord, Master Willem van Outhoorn, Governor General, and the noble Esteemed Lords Councillors of the Netherlands Indies, Your Excellencies, stern, great and respected, valiant, wise, prudent and most generous, highly beloved Lords. On the 10th of December of the past year 1693, we have sent to Your Excellencies the last-mentioned closed business and wage books, etc., which had also encountered difficulties. For this reason they are being sent herewith, the amount of the general expenses from Palembang, the 20th of February, Year 1694, per the ship the Pepper Garden, last mentioned, and at that time we humbly advised Your Excellencies that we intended to have the sloop Laplandt, which required necessary carpentry work, follow with our closed business and wage books, etc., whereby it has unfortunately taken longer than intended and encountered delays, as we had hoped or thought it would not. This was partly because the Jambi account books only reached us in November, and partly because the resident Bolton, with the death of the second person, had to settle and close everything alone without the least assistance. We humbly request that Your High Excellencies will kindly accept this our excuse and apology in good part and believe that such delay was not caused by

--- CHUNK 1 ---
The matter has been delayed longer than was hoped or expected, both because the Jambi account books only reached us later, and because Resident Bolton, following the death of the second person, had to arrange and close everything entirely alone without the slightest assistance. We humbly request that Your High Excellencies be pleased to interpret this excuse and apology of ours in the best light, and to believe that this has not come about through negligence or lack of diligence, but rather that as much speed as possible has been made given the circumstances of the time. According to Your High Excellencies' esteemed mandate for the future, we shall without fail ensure that these accounts are ready in November and shall be sent in a timely manner. The general expenses, both here at the Comptoir [trading post] as well as at the settlement Jambi [Jambi] in one full year, or from the first of August 1692 to the last of July 1693, amount, as appears from the aforementioned books, to a sum of ƒ40,354:— 12 [Dutch guilders]. Namely, among which are some new carpentry work as in other years previously and the profits increased from Palembang on the 20th of February in the year 1694. The aforementioned sort Lapland now go over the Jambi weapons and cannons &c. repaired and made serviceable; and since the remaining ones here are likewise of little use, we have, at the request of our departing general, appointed a few in their place, which we humbly request may be fulfilled at your High Excellencies' convenience at a more suitable time. The well-known Radin Wiera Sarie, alias Macassar, of whom we have previously advised your High Excellencies in detail regarding Radin Macassar Sugatie, that he had fled and, according to the report of Pangeran Area, had gone to the islands of Billiton with 6 vessels, bringing with him 17 Chinese who had lost their junk in the islands of Billiton, of which 16 Chinese still remained there. From the aforementioned Radin Macassar of Palembang on the 20th of February in the year 1694, he departed in order to strengthen himself there with a band of scoundrels, with murder and robbery to make the sea here and there unsafe, or otherwise to flee to Java and the murderer Souropattij, he appeared here again at the end of the previous month of January at Palembang, with six common vessels, together manned with 50 men, also bringing 17 Chinese who, with their junk and 35 persons strong, coming from Borneo, had lost the same on one of the Billiton islands in the same manner, and on the same reef as that of which we owed your High Excellencies notification through the Gideon dated the 29th of October last, the remaining 16 of their countrymen were left there because of the little space in the said vessels and stood by another occasion to come here by way of Moddie, hoping to arrive. We had no other thoughts than that this Radin Macassar would, according to the broad report of Pangeran Area, be seized immediately upon his arrival and, as a pirate and corsair, be punished, but as it has been truthfully reported to us, Radin Macassar upon his return arranged his affairs

Pangeran Rato of Palembang on the 20th of February in the year 1694 has assured them of this in such a way that they cannot refrain from it, except that it becomes clear from this what reliance one can place on their promises and assertions. From Jambi we have, since our last mentioned, received three more letters from Jambi dated the 8th of December, 17th, and 21st of January last, the first and second by inland vessel, and the last with the Chaloupe Paleacatta, which we had sent there on the 16th of December with the requested two thousand rixdollars [modern equivalent: Dutch currency] in cash, but due to the stormy weather and the loss of one [vessel], because of the bad weather, the anchor was first cast on the 17th of January at Jambi, and after the cash was unloaded, it was sent back here with a safe-conduct letter; what we have written there to the resident Real and council, the copy enclosed herein will show, which we have conducted with reverence, your High Excellencies can understand, and likewise the writings of their

The mentioned envoy appears to have returned without accomplishing his business, also to attend a certain wedding feast here at Jang the Pertouan with 2 servants of his, showing the same to Pangeran Rato, which was also done for his brother Pangeran Bevegten Nicabouw. Pangeran Rato's envoy returned from Johoor. An English ship that had been at Johoor for trade had returned to Malacca. --- CHUNK 1 ---
to depart there with a license. With 16 praus [a type of sailing vessel] he had sent toward the river Tambetsij [Tambelan Islands] under the pretext of obtaining some information about taxation there. Pangeran Rato, sent from Johor, had returned with some small vessels. An English ship that had been at Johor for trade had departed again toward Malacca. From Palembang, the 20th of February, Anno 1694. From the 10th of December last, in which the aforementioned Laxamana was also mentioned, we have made special inquiry here into this matter and its conduct; but we could obtain no other understanding, namely that some Johorese rebels with a number of approximately 30 sturdy vessels that were staying thereabouts were causing considerable trouble to the Swahili traders, and that Taxamana, being known as a good warrior and seaman, was sent by order of the king with an army of approximately 40 vessels to drive away these rovers and, if possible, destroy them. What further comes of this remains unknown to us, and the course of time must reveal it. From Jambi under date the 15th of March in the year 1694, concerning the Sultan Ingalaga, to which end the Pangeran Pringabaija places his hope and trust wholly next to God upon his Excellency and upon Your Excellencies' good favor, so that the Sultan Ingalaga may come again to the fallen city of Jambi, and thereby bring the same to its former flourishing state. However, in case the Sultan Ingalaga does not come to appear at Jambi, then certainly the considerable power of the Company and also of their Excellencies' high honor will thereby come to diminish notably, and likewise my person shall come entirely onto the wrong path. Finally, the Pangeran Pringabaija has sent nothing else to the Esteemed Lord Director General Joan van Hoorn than merely a hand-woven cloth with gold mounting, with respectful request that this trifle, as a common flower sprig, may be pleased to accept with favor. — Translation of a Malay missive by Pangeran Pringabaija at Jambi sent to the former king of Jambi Sultan Ingalaga received at Batavia in April in the year 1694. This humble submission of his Majesty's lowly son Pangeran Pringabaija is hereby offered at the feet [of the recipient].
